## Question

Which frog and toad families contain the most species in the AmphibiaWeb data?

## Data

The data come from the [TidyTuesday project](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2026/2026-10-13) and were collected by [AmphibiaWeb](https://amphibiaweb.org/).
Each row represents one frog or toad species.

```{r}
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)

frogs <- read_csv(
  "frogs_and_toads_amphibiaweb.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

## Visualization

```{r}
top_families <- frogs |>
  filter(!is.na(family)) |>
  count(family, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

ggplot(top_families, aes(x = reorder(family, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4F8A5B") +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.2) +
  coord_flip() +
  ylim(0, 1200) +
  labs(
    title = "Families with the most frog and toad species",
    subtitle = "Hylidae has more than 1,000 species in the AmphibiaWeb data",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of species",
    caption = "TidyTuesday 2026-10-13 | Source: AmphibiaWeb"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

Hylidae is the largest family in the dataset with 1,086 species.
Strabomantidae and Microhylidae follow with 840 and 768 species.
The differences show that frog and toad species are not distributed evenly across families.
